result.slice: ADDENDUM 12: the ten writer rules W1–W10 and the chair's rulings R-i, R-ii, R-iii, R-iv, R-vi, R-viii′ (as amended) — re-classified under ADDENDUM 14 (non-contradiction, not licence). 16 items: SPLIT 3 · STRUCK 13 · CONTRADICTION 0 · MODEL 0 · SCOPE 0.

items.gist: THE THREAD AT k=0 — a spine's second sentence must carry a noun forward from its first regardless of k; a face reading as if something precedes it FAILS.
items.ground: No field. Its grounds were the owner's taste row (FOLD 62, 'adjacent sentences connect') and the writer's blindness to k. Where the thread is load-bearing the ENGINE already holds it mechanically: src/domain/prose/passageShapes.js:22-30 makes the 'sentence-then-spine' shape lawful ONLY where the added face carries a noun into the spine, and lawfulPassageShapes selects among the already-lawful rather than repairing a drawn shape. A writer may now connect two sentences by rhythm, image or implication and need not re-seat the settlement name in every sentence; thread goes to the exemplar pack as taste.

items.gist: A negated surface on a PRESENT read is not an absence opener (MOVE-GRAMMAR wall 3); at most ONE such opener per variant.
items.ground: The permissive half (two faces converted to PASS) is moot under the re-cut; the residual bar is the one-per-variant cap, which names no field, and the typed move vocabulary is checked mechanically in src/domain/prose/moveGrammar.js (the owned arms did not red). A writer may now open any number of variants on a negated surface ('No one has needed the bar in a year'), bounded only by W2's totality rule and floor 2.

items.gist: 'asks little of its {defwork}' is NOT the monsterThreat read — a usage frame, a standpoint the card refuses; state the threat in the COUNTRY's terms.
items.ground: Pure licence bookkeeping: it ruled what counts as STATING a read, feeding a density accounting that is no longer a refuter's finding, and 'the card refuses this standpoint' is exactly 'the card does not license it'. A writer may now write the town's own demand on its wall, the townsfolk's habit toward it, the wall as furniture or burden. The one live edge is W2's kept half: an ease claim that becomes a totality still meets the same-page rows.

items.gist: Order alone does not carry the [unfolding] angle — the unfolding variant must realise the OPEN move ('stands open', 'stands unmet', 'is owed').
items.ground: The angle tag and MOVE line are typed metadata no reader sees; ADDENDUM 14 leaves the wave gate only its mechanical duties (projector, variant and face counts, tag grammar, the two tests), and realisation quality is prose judgment. Striking it also cures a measured tic: 'stands open' / 'stands unmet' became house vocabulary. A writer may now realise an angle by image, pacing or attention; the tag stays on the row and the sentence need not wear it.

items.gist: THE ROLL — the office's own formula is lawful, but the roll as an AGENT-SOURCE ('The roll shows…') cites a source the budget does not license.
items.ground: Not merely unlicensed — positively supported. The holder table makes 'muster' a record-keeping kind and cites the muster ROLL as the holder of the walls, garrison, militia, mercenary and charter fields (src/domain/prose/holderTable.js:71, :187-199). The budget objection was licence accounting. A writer may now say 'the roll shows', 'the roll has not been called since', 'whoever keeps the roll keeps it loosely'; only floor 2 binds — the roll may never show a COUNT or a DATE.

items.gist: ONE PURSE — the shortfall lies on the wall's keeping AND the muster's wages alike and the {defwork} STANDS THROUGH it (never 'keeps itself', never paid while the muster is not); AND never that the muster thins, deserts or is undermanned (DS-DEF-5's cell).
items.field: defenseProfile.scores.military via milUpkeepMult — src/generators/defenseGenerator.js:182-192 (one multiplier min(1, 0.6 + econOutput/50 × 0.4) over 'garrison wages, wall maintenance' together, applied to the funded portion above the unpaid community baseline; the recorded rule at :184-186 is that built walls keep standing)
items.keptAs: FLOOR 4 (MODEL), exactly as ADDENDUM 14 names it: one purse over the wall's keeping and the muster's wages, so a face may not write a wall that pays for itself, needs no pay, or is kept whole while the wages are short; and the wall STANDS THROUGH the shortfall, because built walls never fall out of the record for want of coin.
items.struckPart: The bar on saying the muster thins, deserts or is undermanned. That was a cell-overlap rule (R-DST-A, DS-DEF-5 owns the armed-forces surface), not a truth: the generator's own comment at :184-186 says 'unpaid soldiers desert slowly' and milUpkeepMult actually REDUCES the funded force, so slow thinning is model-TRUE. A writer may now show men drifting off, the roll thinner than it was, posts unfilled — with no number (floor 2), no total collapse (the floor is 0.6, never zero), and the shortfall lying on the stonework as well.
items.ground: Floor 4 names R-viii′ explicitly, so the purse half survives as a model rule with a named multiplier; the headcount half was a programme composition rule with no field behind it and is struck cleanly.

items.gist: POSSESSOR BINDING — a possessive after a {defwork}-subject clause binds to that object ('its muster' = the wall's muster); seat the town as possessor or drop the possessive.
items.ground: The record does not deny the relation, it CARRIES it: src/domain/prose/holderTable.js:188-193 files walls, garrison, militia, mercenary and charter under ONE holder kind — the muster roll — so the wall and the men under arms are the same record in this engine. A grammar-binding rule with no field behind it. A writer may now use 'its muster', 'the wall's men', 'the gate's watch' as flavour. The one residue is mechanical and belongs to the composer, not the writer (see new finding 1).

items.gist: THE THREAT IS COUNTRY-SCOPED — state the monsterThreat read over the country, never as a totality over the town ('nothing threatens {settlement}'), because DS-DEF-2 carries war pressures on the same page (C7).
items.field: the 'Invasion & War' row of buildThreatAssessment — src/domain/display/threatAssessment.js:113-130, rendered beside this block at src/components/new/tabs/DefenseTab.jsx:150-183; and config.monsterThreat's tier arithmetic at src/generators/stressGenerator.js:121, :168, :231
items.keptAs: FLOOR 1 (CONTRADICTION): a TOTALITY of safety over the town is denied twice on the same screen. (a) the Invasion & War row prints for every town — an unwalled town reads 'Cannot resist organized military aggression', a militia town 'inadequate against any professional force with siege capability'. (b) the tier the QUIET pool keys on is LOW, never NONE: heartland multiplies monster 0.3, occupation 0.4 and war 0.4, never zero (ADDENDUM 13A item 4 already corrected 'settled' to the low tier). So 'nothing threatens {settlement}', 'the town has nothing to fear', 'there is no danger here' stay refusable, with the row named.
items.struckPart: The requirement that the read be PHRASED over the country — one of the audit's measured tics ('country' once every 21 words). A writer may now write ease at the town's own grain: 'the bar has not been dropped in years', 'children play on the earthwork', 'the gate stands open more often than not'.
items.ground: The finding class was real and same-page; only its prescribed phrasing was construction.

items.gist: THE BAND MARKER — a tier band carries its marker ('village size or under'); the bare value is a value and contradicts the head record on the other tiers of the band.
items.field: settlement.tier as printed on the identity strip — src/components/new/tabs/OverviewTab.jsx:247 ({r.tier}, capitalised, beside the name and population); the band spans are on the card's STATE-KEY line, docs/content/RECEIPT_POOLS_DOSSIER_STATE.md:6200 (UNWALLED-SMALL = village and below; UNWALLED-LARGE = town and above)
items.keptAs: FLOOR 1 (CONTRADICTION): DS-DEF-11 targets defense AND overview, so a band-wide face saying 'the village' on a Thorp, or 'the town' on a Metropolis, is denied by the tier word printed on the strip above it.
items.struckPart: The requirement to SPELL the band ('village size or under', 'a town or larger') — receipt language and a measured tic. A writer may now write around the tier word entirely ('a place this size', 'too small for stone', 'no circuit for a place this big'), or use the recorded tier word where the pool fires on one tier only.
items.ground: The contradiction is with a printed field; the marker prescription was construction.

items.gist: THE CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT — the draft's declared grammar per variant is the refiner's to keep; moving a variant onto its sibling's construction is a regression.
items.ground: No field and no truth claim: a fidelity rule about the drafting pipeline's own stages. Its real subject — a pool collapsing into one construction — is re-pointed to the instrument ADDENDUM 14 creates, the pool-grain CRAFT verdict (a collapsed pool is sent back as DULL). A writer may now rewrite a variant onto any construction that serves it, including its sibling's, when the sibling's is better; the constraint is judged at the pool, never charged against a face.

items.gist: THE NAMING-FORM ARTICLE — 'the town of {settlement}' is the naming form; a frame needing the generic article to carry a band ('a town of X's weight') is a maxim frame.
items.ground: A tone bar against the maxim voice, with no field behind it; the one true edge inside it is the tier word, which survives as W3's kept half. A writer may now use 'a town of {settlement}'s weight', 'a place like this one', generic articles and comparatives freely — only the tier the identity strip prints binds.

items.gist: NO DOUBLED BEAT — a clause that restates the read it follows is the summarising beat.
items.ground: Tone, with no field. Re-pointed to the pool-grain CRAFT verdict: repetition is dullness, judged as craft, never a lawfulness finding. A writer may now repeat for rhythm and land a beat twice where the second landing earns it.

items.gist: THE ROLL (= R-vi): the roll may not be cited as an agent-source.
items.ground: As R-vi, and positively refuted rather than merely unenforced: the muster roll is a modelled record-keeper (src/domain/prose/holderTable.js:71, :187-199). A writer may now show, cite, characterise, doubt or neglect the roll; it may never be made to show a count or a date (floor 2).

items.gist: THE ANGLES — the unfolding realises OPEN; the visitor carries the gate only as the wall's standing state ('kept at full cost'), never as the town's act or an accounts fact; the ledger enters and measures, and cites nothing.
items.ground: Three tone rules stacked: an angle-realisation rule (R-iv, struck), a standpoint refusal (R-iii's class, struck) and the citation bar (R-vi, struck and positively refuted by the holder table). No field behind any of the three. A writer may now let the visitor see the town spending on its wall, let the ledger cite its own source, and reach the gate from any angle — with the gate itself still under R-viii′ (one purse) and floor 2 (no sums).

items.gist: ENTAILMENTS ARE MAY, NEVER MUST — the density floor counts the card's reads, not the entailment table's attributes.
items.ground: A meta-rule about how another rule counts; it never policed truth. Under ADDENDUM 14 the table it protected is re-pointed from 'what may be said' to 'what would be false', so nothing in it can compel a writer in either direction, and the density floor it guarded (ADDENDUM 6) is itself no longer a refuter's finding. A writer may now ignore attribute counting entirely and consult the table only to ask whether a sentence is FALSE.

items.gist: A NEGATED SURFACE ON A PRESENT READ is not an absence opener, one per variant (R-ii).
items.ground: As R-ii: the one-per-variant cap names no field and the typed move vocabulary is a mechanical arm. A writer may now open on negation as often as the pool wants variety; only W2's totality rule and floor 2's invented facts bind.

newFindings: A face-initial possessive or pronoun binds to ANOTHER DESK'S subject at composition. W1 charged this inside one face, where the holder table makes it harmless; the live case is the composed passage — the composer joins a spine and up to k added sentences from other pools (composeStateProse.js:679, the fact budget k <= 3 - |spine.reads|), so a face opening 'Its muster …' can land after a granary or market sentence and assert a possession the record gives no such body. It is a COMPOSITION defect, not a writer's fault, and its cure is mechanical — refuse the SHAPE, as passageShapes.js already refuses 'sentence-then-spine' without a carried noun. For the register car.

The town's AGE is printed, so history is now a live CONTRADICTION source rather than only a silence. The identity strip prints '{hist.age} years old' and a historicalCharacter line (OverviewTab.jsx:251, :259). DS-DEF-11's card recorded 'when the wall was raised has NO backing fact and is deliberately absent' — a licence argument, void under ADDENDUM 14. What replaces it is sharper: age-flavour is free EXCEPT where it contradicts the printed age or character. A wall 'raised in living memory' on a four-hundred-year-old town is a floor-1 breach against a number on the same page.

There are FOUR upkeep gates on the defense page, not two, and they are monotone in ONE input, so a face may never split their DIRECTION. Military 0.6 (defenseGenerator.js:189), monster 0.7 (:223), internal/order 0.65 (:251), disaster 0.55 (:614) — each min(1, floor + econOutput/50 × (1-floor)). ADDENDUM 12's amendment stated the one-purse pattern WITHIN a class and named two purses; the cross-gate rule follows and was never written: at birth no face may say one funded arm is flush while another starves (the watch paid and the muster not, patrols provisioned and the gaol unfunded). They differ in degree only, never in direction.

The shortfall is BOUNDED, so a face may not write a total collapse of pay. Every gate has a floor and the unpaid community baseline is exempt entirely (defenseGenerator.js:186-192). 'Nothing has been paid in a year', 'the wages stopped', 'there is no watch left to pay' contradict the model even on the poorest town; the licensed extreme is short, late or thin — never none. This is the boundary on the half of R-viii′ this fold strikes.

The engine's own contradiction module treats tension as a FEATURE — evidence for the re-cut, and a bar on flattening. src/domain/contradictions.js:136-153 detects a cathedral in a hamlet and classifies it 'interesting_tension', emitting consequences and hooks rather than a defect. A face that explains a tension away ('nothing here is out of place') can therefore contradict a surface the same dossier prints.

The same page calls the defwork a PALISADE regardless of what the wall row records. threatAssessment.js:59, :66, :80 hardcode 'Palisade and citizen militia' and 'The palisade creates a chokepoint' on branches that fire for any institutions.walls row, including 'Town walls', 'citadel' and 'massive walls' (defenseInstitutionBuckets.js:84-86). It is product code (OW-20's class, outside the REWRITE's corpus) but it is a floor-1 self-contradiction on the rendered page and it directly undercuts the sibling slice's re-cut of the MATERIAL bar (W11): the rewrite can be made correct about the wall's material while the row beside it says palisade. For the owner via the register car.

items.gist: THE LAYER BAR: a noun is used at the layer of its READ; a body word on an AGGREGATE or NONE read is refused (a readiness band, safety label, score band, capture rung, stock band or terrain token names no watch, garrison, wall, granary, hall or market)
items.field: inst.hasWatch / hasGarrison / hasMilitia / hasMercenary / hasWalls / hasCharterHall / hasGranary / hasMarket
items.ground: KEPT half is the label trap and it has a field: getInstitutionNames computes the force flags from the live roster (src/generators/priorityHelpers.js:45-60) and src/generators/safetyProfile.js:281-300 prints the enforcement noun FROM those flags on the same page, falling to 'Local enforcement' (:281), 'Locals watch over' (:289) and the flat denial 'There is no meaningful guard presence.' (:300). D-F2 of REFERENT-TABLE 5.1 is FALSE exactly where the flag is false (thorp/hamlet/village, a ruined-watch town). The layer discipline itself has no field behind it: nothing denies that a band read may be narrated through a body the town actually holds.
items.keptAs: A face may not seat a body the town's roster denies — no watch, garrison, militia, hall, granary or market word where the corresponding inst.has* flag is false, because the safety panel prints the fallback sentence beside it.
items.struckPart: The layer-matching rule itself. A band, label, rung, stock or terrain read may now be narrated through the bodies the roster does hold — 'the watch feels the badge before the town does' is lawful on a town with a watch.

items.gist: THE BAKED-POWER BAR: never 'the hall', 'the council', 'the chamber', 'the seat's people' as the power; the power is the {seat} slot or the class words 'the ruling structure' / 'the seat'
items.ground: KEPT: the seat's own label is a field — governingName = government = the governing faction's label ('Town Mayor', "Headman's Authority", 'Elder Council', 'Merchant Council': src/generators/power/rulingStructure.js:264-300, :783-790) and the Power tab prints it; 'the hall' as a building is denied where no hall row stands (inst.hasCourtSystem's name list, priorityHelpers.js:55). STRUCK: the closed class-word list policed permission only, and it bit hardest where the record is silent — the census reports {seat} NAMED BUT NEVER FILLED (W-2).
items.keptAs: A power word the seat's own record denies: a council where governingName is a mayor or a headman, a hall where the roster holds no hall.
items.struckPart: The requirement to name the power only through {seat} or two approved class words. A writer may now say the hall, the chamber, the seat's people, the long table.

items.gist: the six ruling-power words (autocrat · council · theocracy · merchant_league · criminal · mixed) are lens VALUES, safe only as the pool they key, never as a body
items.ground: The classification is TOTAL and fails soft to 'mixed', so it positively fixes the KIND of every town's power. Naming a kind the lens denies (a council on an autocrat town, a temple rule on a merchant_league town) contradicts the value the pool is keyed on and the seat label it derives from. 'Never as a body' beyond that was pure layer hygiene.
items.keptAs: A power KIND the lens value or the seat label denies.
items.struckPart: The blanket rule that a lens value may never be spoken as a thing in the town — a council that meets, a temple that rules, a syndicate that collects is now lawful where the lens holds it.

items.gist: on a CAPTURE read the CLASS WORD replaces {seat} until seatKind lands (OW-3: the slot can render a ROLE or a standing-laden label as the organ)
items.ground: KEPT and generalised (NF-1): the fill can be 'Corrupt Council', 'Corrupt City Council', 'Shadow Senate' (rulingStructure.js:245-256, :264-283), so a clause negating the standing the fill asserts contradicts itself at render time — D-F27's 'Nothing criminal has reached the {seat}'. STRUCK: banning the slot was a hedge against a fill the writer cannot see, not a truth condition.
items.keptAs: A clause may not argue against what the rendered slot's own words assert.
items.struckPart: The substitution of a class word for {seat} on capture reads; the slot is usable again.

items.gist: THE PERSON BAR (agent half): no person as agent, decider, holder of a permission, chooser or load-bearing referent ('somebody', 'whoever', 'the person who', 'the clerks record', 'the collectors travel')
items.ground: ADDENDUM 14 floor 3 relaxes W22 by name: 'an UNNAMED person may appear, act, keep a key, be avoided, be resented. A reeve who is slow to open the books is a plot hook and is now LICENSED.' No field denies an unnamed actor; the engine models institutions, not the absence of people. Nineteen of the defense desk's twenty-eight wrong-layer findings (D-F6…D-F15 and others) were this bar alone.
items.struckPart: A writer may now put people in the town: somebody keeps the key to the gate-house; whoever is on the book that night decides what gets looked at; the collectors take the long way round.

items.gist: the ROLE instrument: a role word only where the engine EMITS the office (officesOf · ROLE_FACTION_MAP · FACTION_ROLES · TIER_MANDATORY_ROLES); 'clerk', 'collector', 'officer', 'administrator', 'scout', 'heir' have no row and are refused
items.ground: The engine says the opposite in its own words at src/domain/institutions/institutionTable.js:370-376: 'THE COLUMN IS OPEN AND STAYS OPEN. The structural NPC roster is a SAMPLE (one to three per faction by its own header), so a town has offices the roster does not name. That is not a gap to be filled; it is what makes the column open.' An unrostered office contradicts nothing.
items.struckPart: A writer may name any office the town would plausibly keep. The only residue is W20's: a title that ENTAILS a body the roster denies (a garrison commander with no garrison row) fails as a label trap, not as a role word.

items.gist: no NAMED character's fate; a recorded {npc} NAME prints as a name with no predicate on the person
items.ground: Floor 3, unchanged — product scope and THE PROMISE (never a NAMED character's fate). The two lit {npc} routes are recorded names only: ladderRead.js:95-107 and generalStateProse.js:1502 ('never minted, no fate resolved').
items.keptAs: A recorded name may stand; a named person's fate, consequential decision or end may not.

items.gist: 'Corrupt Official' is a public role string, never a standing a face may infer
items.ground: The role is MANDATED and rostered openly under the occupied / insurgency stresses (src/generators/npcGenerator.js:1511-1532, :1524), and REFERENT-TABLE 4.2 records that 'the roster names the corrupt officer OPENLY'. Reading a standing off a string the page prints in public is agreement with the page, not invention.
items.struckPart: A face may say the town knows one of its officials is bought, where the roster prints one. The real fault runs the other way — see newFinding NF-2.

items.gist: THE FUSED-AGENT BAR: no relation between two referents that no field computes ('the bought watch is paid short', 'the town has decided', 'the hall moves against the operators and the operators move back', 'the resistance is bleeding the garrison'); two facts are two units, one referent per unit
items.ground: This bar is exactly 'the record does not compute it', which ADDENDUM 14 converts to permission. No field DENIES a relation; the four typed causes of institutionStatusModel.js:118-120 are what a world-run cell may CITE, never a closed list of what may be described. The one-referent-per-unit half is a construction rule — tone, not truth.
items.struckPart: Two things may now act on each other: the hall leans on the operators; the town has made its peace with the toll. The residue sits elsewhere — a TERM naming a body the roster denies fails under W20, and a relation asserting a corruption the page denies fails under NF-2.

items.gist: THE RECORD-WORD BAR (the whitelist): an ORGAN read may use only its kind's ratified nouns (books · purse · chest · roll · register · word · memory …), never accounts · returns · duties · ledgers · manifests · minutes · the writ · a licence
items.ground: A vocabulary list with no field behind it. Nothing in the engine denies that a treasury keeps accounts or a court keeps minutes; the ratified list was assembled from what the holder table could PROVE, which is the old licence test.
items.struckPart: Accounts, ledgers, minutes, returns, manifests and the writ are all back in the writer's hands.

items.gist: on a read that resolves NO holder (SOURCE-UNRESOLVED), no record word at all; 'the rolls' on a population read is refused
items.field: inst.hasMilitia / hasGarrison / hasMarket (priorityHelpers.js:45-60); the A13 'holder with no institution' branch
items.ground: KEPT: the arm's own branch names the real fault — 'a holder with no institution … the holder kind resolves to no institution in this town's roster, so the cited record has nobody keeping it' (src/domain/prose/composedWalker.js:1071-1073). A toll book where no toll-bar stands, a muster roll where neither militia nor garrison resolves, is the label trap in record clothing. STRUCK: the silence-about-the-holder rule.
items.keptAs: A record word whose KEEPER the town's roster denies.
items.struckPart: 'The rolls', 'the book', 'the count' may be written freely on any read whose keeper the town actually has, resolved by the card or not.

items.gist: the [ledger] ANGLE is a STANDPOINT and licenses NO record noun and no citation ('the books show' is a citation; only the office's own formula is lawful)
items.ground: Arm A13 states its own nature in its report row: a citation 'is a PROVENANCE move and spends a budget the sitting has not yet set' (src/domain/prose/composedWalker.js:1051-1052). A budget is not a truth condition, and no surface denies that a ledger face may quote its own record.
items.struckPart: 'The books show a purse that does not stretch' is lawful. A ledger face may cite, measure and quote.

items.gist: THE EXTERNAL-BODY BAR: a foreign force is named with its possessor stated ('the occupier's men', 'the besieger'); never a bare 'the garrison' for the occupier's force, never '{counterpart}'s garrison'
items.field: worldState.occupations[id] = {occupierId, state, resistance} — no garrison field; inst.hasGarrison
items.ground: src/domain/display/occupationStatus.js:74-96 shows the occupation record carries occupierId, state and resistance and NO force field, while 'the garrison' is the occupied town's own roster row (src/generators/priorityHelpers.js:46). A bare 'the garrison' for the occupier asserts that the town's own body is the occupier's — denied by the roster panel and by the occupation record on the same page.
items.keptAs: The bar stands whole: an external force is named with its possessor, and the town's own body words are never lent to it.

items.gist: on a TREATY pool {counterpart} is the martial counterpart and never the signatory, so no possessor is stated through it
items.ground: src/domain/display/stateProse/warFaithStateProse.js:930-932 (and the type note at :690-694) resolves {counterpart} to the occupier or the ONE siege party; the treaty document's sides are a separate structure (treatyDocument.js:359-361). Attributing a treaty's terms, signature or intent to {counterpart} names the wrong party on the rendered page.
items.keptAs: The bar stands whole; side-neutral cells and {term} remain the safe forms until OW-9's wiring lands.

items.gist: 'Unknown Faction (hidden)' through {counterpart} on a player face is a wiring defect, and a writer treats {counterpart} on DS-POW-4 as DM-only until it is fixed
items.ground: A properFill defect, not a prose fault (stressFactions.js:105-107; rulingPowerCoup.js:51, :104; powerStateProse.js:178-186; logged as a register row in REFERENT-TABLE 4.2). A writer can neither cause nor cure it, and no face is false because of it.
items.struckPart: {counterpart} faces may be written for the player face on DS-POW-4; filtering the literal '(hidden)' string is the register car's job.

items.gist: THE VISIBILITY BAR: a birth capture at corrupted/capture, a covert impairment, a covert posture, a covert bloc, foreign funding and the attacker's identity are the DM face; the player face says what the state's organs would admit and may say the town does NOT KNOW
items.field: impairments[].covert; blocs[].covert; mobilization covert; brokeragePatronage covert + the player projection's patronName:'unknown'; audience = playerView ? 'player' : 'dm'
items.ground: Floor 4: the engine positively models audience. src/domain/corruption.js:667-691 (covert impairment and the unexposed-stooge route), settlementPolitics.js:423-436, mobilization.js:128 and :147, src/domain/worldPulse/brokeragePatronage.js:296 with the player projection writing patronName 'unknown' at :326, and the caller gate at PowerTab.jsx:194-215 where publicDossier nulls the whole desk. A player face naming a covert fact denies the projection printed beside it.
items.keptAs: Covert reads stay on the DM face; the player face keeps the positive move the bar always allowed and nobody used — the town DOES NOT KNOW, and the not-knowing is the hook.

items.gist: a citing player face on an INTERESTED holder fails (arm A13), so a player face never cites a state organ's record where the town is captured
items.ground: A13's FAIL text is a licence rule resting on a provenance budget ('the holder of this record is a power with an interest in it', src/domain/prose/composedWalker.js:1077-1079), and REFERENT-TABLE 4.2 records that NO product caller resolves the arm at draw time. Nothing on the page denies that a captured town's court still keeps a roll.
items.struckPart: A player face may cite the organ in a captured town. An interested record read aloud by a player face is unreliable narration — the most usable plot hook in the slice.

items.gist: THE ANGLE-TAG BAR (body half): the seven tags are STANCES, not bodies; 'the elders' as a body only where the elders kind resolves
items.field: the roster flags of priorityHelpers.js:45-60 (the elders / watch / market rows)
items.ground: KEPT: naming a body the roster denies is W20's contradiction wearing a stance's clothes. STRUCK: 'a tag licenses nothing' is a permission rule; a stance's idiom denies no field.
items.keptAs: A stance may not seat a body the town's roster denies.
items.struckPart: A stance may now reach for its own nouns and its own rhythm — [street] may talk like a street, [elder] like an elder.

newFindings: NF-1 A RENDERED SLOT'S OWN WORDS BIND THE CLAUSE AROUND IT. A `proper` slot may render a STANDING-LADEN label — {seat} can be 'Corrupt Council', 'Corrupt City Council', 'Shadow Senate' (src/generators/power/rulingStructure.js:245-256, :264-283); {counterpart} can be 'Military/Guard', 'War Council', 'Conversion Enforcement Office' (stressFactions.js:105-107). A clause that negates or argues against what the fill asserts contradicts itself AT RENDER TIME ('Nothing criminal has reached the Corrupt Council of X'). This generalises D-F27 from one pool to every slot-bearing face on every desk and is a refuter's finding with a field.

NF-2 A FACE THAT DENIES A CORRUPTION THE PAGE PRINTS. W22d policed the inference; the contradiction runs the other way and was never written down. Under the occupied / insurgency stresses the NPC roster MANDATES a 'Corrupt Official' (src/generators/npcGenerator.js:1511-1532), and a REVEALED corruption impairment is a public scandal (src/domain/corruption.js:654-658, :679). A face asserting clean hands, an unbought office or an unreachable seat on such a town is denied by the roster beside it.

NF-3 THE SAFETY PANEL DENIES THE FORCE'S STATE, NOT ONLY ITS EXISTENCE. W20 policed only the body NOUN. src/generators/safetyProfile.js:296-300 prints the force's CONDITION in the engine's own words — 'The garrison is overwhelmed or corrupt.' / 'The watch is stretched far beyond its capacity.' / 'The militia cannot maintain consistent coverage.' / 'There is no meaningful guard presence.' — and :281-289 the opposite at the safe bands. A dossier face with the watch comfortably covering the lanes beside :297, or a slack watch beside :281, is a same-page contradiction with a quotable sentence. It cuts both ways, so it also tells a writer which mood is licensed on which band: the richest untapped finding class in this slice.

NF-4 A POOLED FACE IS WRITTEN ONCE AND DRAWN BY MANY TOWNS. Any proper noun a face carries that is not borne by a slot — a person, a tavern, a lane, a family — prints identically in every town that draws that pool. No per-town field denies it, so no licence test would ever have caught it. It is a cross-town identity collision and belongs in the refuters' instrument as its own class; it is the real ground under W27b's 'never be given a name'.

NF-5 `plagued` CARRIES A CONSEQUENCE, NOT ONLY A CAUSE. Floor 4 already says plagued is monsters and never disease; the engine goes further on the same page — at the safest band safetyProfile.js:276 prints 'The constant monster threat keeps the guard exceptionally well-drilled and alert.' A plagued face writing a cowed, sickened or demoralised town contradicts the panel beside it wherever that branch fires.

NF-6 THE OCCUPIER IS SPELLED TWO WAYS ON TWO SURFACES. occupierName = nameFor(rec.occupierId) is a foreign TOWN's name (src/domain/display/occupationStatus.js:83-96), while the map overlay spells the occupier as the OCCUPIED town's installed governingName or the literal 'occupation authority' (warStatus.js:318-335; pulseKernel.js:1150). A face naming one where the surface beside it prints the other is a same-page mismatch — a register-car wiring row as much as a writer's finding, recorded so the refuters do not charge the writer for it.

THE READINESS BAND MOVES ON THINGS THAT ARE NOT THE WORKS. readiness = avgScore + tierBonus - threatPenalty (defenseGenerator.js:510), so the band can drop while every wall, gate and roster row is unchanged.
